answer_text:
Because

\[
T_{ijkl}=T_{jikl}=T_{ijlk},
\]

the first pair \((i,j)\) can be treated as an **unordered pair** from \(\{1,2,3,4\}\). The number of such unordered pairs is

\[
\binom{4}{2}+4=\binom{4+2-1}{2}=10.
\]

Likewise, the last pair \((k,l)\) is also one of these 10 unordered pairs.

Thus \(T_{ijkl}\) can be viewed as a \(10\times 10\) matrix \(M_{ab}\), where each index \(a,b\) labels one of the 10 symmetric index pairs.

The remaining condition is

\[
T_{ijkl}=-T_{klij},
\]

which says that this \(10\times 10\) matrix is **skew-symmetric**:

\[
M_{ab}=-M_{ba}.
\]

A skew-symmetric \(n\times n\) matrix has zero diagonal and \(\binom{n}{2}\) independent entries. Therefore, with \(n=10\), the number of independent components is

\[
\binom{10}{2}=45.
\]

Hence the number of independent components of \(T_{ijkl}\) is

\[
\boxed{45}.
\]

27B·v4.method: Identify T as a skew-symmetric 10×10 matrix (10 = dim Sym²V), giving C(10,2) = 45 independent components.
